description_html:
Since this is episode one, today is a little different. Instead of just news, I want to give you a map of the whole territory: the handful of ideas that matter if you want to build agents that actually work, plus the most interesting things that have happened in the last few months. Then, starting tomorrow, we'll go deeper, one or two topics at a time.

Highlights

  • tools-and-protocols: MCP 2026-07-28 stateless core, MRTR, cacheable lists, auth hardening.
  • skills: 32 adopters by March 2026; GitSkills 3.8M SKILL.md files; 157 malicious skills found (USENIX Sec 2026).
  • computer-use / evals: OSWorld 2.0 best 20.6% completion; a16z production report.
  • prompt-injection-security / identity: Microsoft "agents are your newest insiders" (Dynamic Permissions, Agent ID); NSA/CISA/NIST control-incident guidance.
  • user-data-safety: ICO call for evidence on agentic AI (closes 2026-11-20).
  • sandboxing: Perplexity open-sourced SPACE (Firecracker microVMs).

title: Episode 2 - The Harness Is the Product
summary: The harness deep dive: the agent loop, the six components, Anthropic's Planner/Generator/Evaluator design, how Codex, Claude Code, Gemini/Antigravity, Cursor, Aider and Goose differ, plus enterprise quality, OpenTelemetry tracing, pass@k vs pass^k, and a first look at voice agents.
description_html:
Episode two is the harness deep dive you asked for. A language model only reads and writes text; the harness is the loop around it that turns it into an agent. We break the harness into six engineerable parts, walk through Anthropic's Planner / Generator / Evaluator design, and compare how the major harnesses differ on safety model, where they run, and extensibility.

Highlights

  • harnesses: the agent loop step by step; six components (execution loop, tool registry, context manager, state store, lifecycle hooks, evaluation interface); Anthropic's sprint contracts and Playwright evaluator; why harness assumptions should be deleted as models improve.
  • harness comparison: Codex CLI (Seatbelt, Landlock/seccomp, network off by default), Claude Code (permissions + optional sandbox), Gemini CLI moving to Antigravity CLI, Cursor cloud VMs, Aider/Goose git-undo, Claude Managed Agents (controller, credentials and logs outside the sandbox); frameworks LangGraph, Pydantic AI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK.
  • enterprise quality / tracing: AICPA + AIUC agent certification (SOC 2 plus live behavioral testing); Harness survey of 700 enterprises (75% in production, 19% eval-gated releases, 33% kill switch); OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions still in development, pin your version.
  • evals: pass@k vs pass^k from Sierra's tau-bench; an 87% single-try agent passes all 5 tries only about half the time.
  • voice agents (new wiki topic): cascaded pipeline vs speech-to-speech, turn detection with LiveKit Agents and Pipecat, OpenAI Realtime and Gemini Live, latency budgets.

Sources
